stories.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, its first frontier model in a while
stories.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, which reportedly beats rival models Astra and Fable on LiveBench. It also cut the runtime of one TypeScript-to-Rust benchmark by 48.6%.
stories.why: A new frontier model that beats rivals on coding-related benchmarks may shift which models teams evaluate and adopt.

sources.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, an AI tool that reviews and approves pull requests
stories.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship in beta. It automatically reviews and corrects suggested code changes and can approve them against a team's guidelines.
stories.why: Automated review and approval of pull requests could change code review workflows and the controls engineering leaders need to set.

sources.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review, fix, and approve pull requests on their own

stories.headline: Anthropic's MCP SDK passes 700 million monthly downloads, adds agent features
stories.summary: Anthropic says its Model Context Protocol SDK now has over 700 million monthly downloads, two years after launch. New features include background tasks, follow-up questions to users, and file uploads for more autonomous agents.
stories.why: MCP is becoming a widely used integration standard, so its new agent features affect how teams connect tools to AI systems.

sources.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents

stories.headline: Amazon says AI agents found and exploited a zero-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon reports that attackers' AI agents discovered and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human direction. It describes the Cairn AI framework as useful to both defenders and attackers.
stories.why: Autonomous exploit discovery shortens the window teams have to patch, which raises the stakes for security practices.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: Insiders say unreleased OpenAI and Anthropic models have outgrown safety measures
stories.summary: According to an Axios report, many employees at OpenAI and Anthropic believe their unreleased frontier models can no longer be safely controlled. Both companies are reportedly debating whether to halt releases or stop training.
stories.why: Concerns about controllability of upcoming models could affect release timing and the reliability of the AI platforms teams depend on.

sources.title: Dozens of insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown their safety measures

stories.headline: PrismML compresses a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB using three-value weights
stories.summary: Startup PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an updated version of its heavily compressed model. Each weight is reduced to one of just three possible values, cutting the size from 54 GB to 5.9 GB.
stories.why: Much smaller models make it more practical to run capable language models on modest hardware and at lower cost.

sources.title: PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values

stories.headline: Active intrusion campaign targets Check Point security management servers
stories.summary: An active intrusion campaign is targeting Check Point security management servers, a topic that drew strong discussion on Hacker News. Operators of these servers should check their exposure and review their security posture.
stories.why: Security management servers control firewall policy across an organisation, so a compromise there can spread to many systems at once.

sources.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers

stories.headline: Fixes released for Java4Shell memory corruption bug in the HotSpot JVM
stories.summary: Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes on November 17 for CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption flaw in the Base64 decoder of the HotSpot JVM. JetBrains has told users to update its IDEs, ReSharper, .NET tools, Toolbox and Gateway.
stories.why: Any Java service or developer tool running an unpatched JVM may be exposed, so teams should check their runtime versions now.

sources.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability: Update Your JetBrains IDEs, ReSharper, .NET Tools, Toolbox App, and Gateway Now

stories.headline: AWS Lambda doubles maximum timeout to 30 minutes
stories.summary: AWS has raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions. No opt-in is needed and there is no new pricing, and AWS notes the change also doubles concurrency at the same request rate.
stories.why: Longer timeouts can simplify workloads that once needed step functions or workarounds, but teams should recheck concurrency and cost assumptions.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
AWS Weekly Roundup: Local Zone in Bogotá, 30-minute Lambda timeout, and more (November 24, 2026)

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type after a decade of work
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released November 12, stabilises the never type (!) and makes Infallible an alias for it. The release also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and gives Cargo an opt-in setting for dependency cooldowns.
stories.why: The never type removes long-standing friction in error handling, and the Cargo cooldown option gives teams a new way to limit fresh dependency updates.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: Confluent scraps AI-driven Rust rewrite of Kafka's Java client
stories.summary: Confluent spent almost three months using AI coding agents to translate Apache Kafka's Java client into Rust. The engineers discarded the work and started over.
stories.why: It shows that agent-driven code translation of large, complex libraries can take far longer than expected and may need to be restarted.

sources.title: Confluent spent 3 months rewriting Kafka’s Java client in Rust with AI — and had to start over

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after nearly 24-hour Outlook outage
stories.summary: Microsoft has declared an unusual internal 'Code Red' after an Exchange Online and Outlook outage that lasted almost a day and disrupted email for millions of customers. Internal memos reportedly describe an overhaul and a goal of one-hour recovery.
stories.why: It shows how a single bug in shared networking infrastructure can take down a major service, and it sets a recovery-time benchmark other platform teams may be judged against.

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”

stories.headline: US jury finds Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquits on racketeering
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York convicted Huawei of stealing US trade secrets, including source code and proprietary technology from several companies, and found it guilty of conspiracy. It acquitted the company on racketeering charges.
stories.why: The verdict concerns theft of source code and proprietary technology, which matters to engineering teams thinking about IP protection and supply-chain trust.

sources.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
Jury finds Huawei stole US tech, laundered money, and broke sanctions
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury rules

stories.headline: Trump says pardoning Jensen Huang is 'an option' amid Nvidia probe
stories.summary: Reports say Donald Trump considers a pardon for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang an option. The US attorney general avoided questions about an investigation into Nvidia, and Nvidia's share price fell 7% as lawmakers demanded answers about Trump's role in Huang's reinstatement.
stories.why: Scrutiny of Nvidia, which dominates AI chip supply, could affect hardware availability, pricing and the regulatory climate for AI infrastructure.

sources.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’

stories.headline: US financial crimes bureau FinCEN investigates unauthorized access to systems
stories.summary: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed a 'cybersecurity incident' that gave unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. It has not released further details.
stories.why: Government breaches involving financial intelligence systems highlight the need for strict access controls and monitoring in internal tools and data platforms.

sources.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’

stories.headline: Dozens of oil and chemical shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks
stories.summary: A report says dozens of oil and chemical shipping vessels have been hit by cyberattacks in recent weeks. Iran is named as the main suspect.
stories.why: Attacks on operational technology at sea show how exposed industrial control and maritime systems are, a reminder for teams securing connected operational systems.

sources.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report

stories.headline: CLI-Anything pitches agent-native command lines for any software
stories.summary: The CLI-Anything project, which describes itself as making all software agent-native and links to a CLI-Hub, gained about 1,070 GitHub stars in a day and has around 65,000 in total. The project is early and its claims are not yet proven.
stories.why: If AI agents can reliably drive existing tools through CLIs, teams may need to rethink how they expose internal software to automation.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: Superpowers agentic skills framework keeps climbing GitHub Trending
stories.summary: obra/superpowers, a framework of agentic skills and a software development methodology, added about 1,000 stars today and has over 326,000 in total. Its popularity signals strong interest in structured workflows for coding agents.
stories.why: Teams adopting coding agents are looking for repeatable methods, and this framework shows how much developers want shared conventions for them.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Claude-BugHunter skill bundle draws a large daily star spike
stories.summary: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work, with 84 skills and 15 slash commands, gained about 1,800 stars today. Its value for real security work has not been independently shown.
stories.why: Security leads should weigh how easily agent-driven offensive tooling spreads, and how it fits their disclosure and authorisation policies.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: Firecrawl pitches one API for search, scraping and 550+ data sources
stories.summary: Firecrawl, which calls itself knowledge infrastructure for agents, added about 990 stars today and has over 209,000 in total. It offers search, scraping and access to more than 550 data providers through a single API.
stories.why: Agent builders are consolidating data access behind single APIs, which can cut integration work but adds a dependency to manage.

sources.title: firecrawl/firecrawl: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

stories.headline: minimind shows a 64M-parameter LLM can be trained from scratch in two hours
stories.summary: The minimind project, which describes training a 64M-parameter language model from scratch in about two hours, gained around 730 stars today and has over 70,000 in total. It is a small educational-style model, not a competitive system.
stories.why: It makes the basics of model training far more approachable for engineers who want to understand LLM internals.

sources.title: jingyaogong/minimind: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO predicts manual code review could end within two years
stories.summary: The JetBrains CEO gives manual code review two years before it becomes obsolete, a claim that puts AI tooling at the centre of how teams review changes.
stories.why: If review shifts to AI, engineering leaders will need to rethink review policies, accountability and how junior engineers learn.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: Less experienced developers trust AI output more, a LeadDev piece says
stories.summary: A LeadDev article reports that less experienced developers place more trust in AI tools, and argues that code ownership is weakening as a result.
stories.why: Leaders who set code ownership norms and mentoring plans need to account for how juniors weigh AI suggestions.

sources.title: Code ownership is eroding

stories.headline: Capital One describes its multi-agent AI system as a platform problem
stories.summary: LeadDev reports on how Capital One built its multi-agent AI system, framing the challenge as one of platform engineering rather than individual tools.
stories.why: It shows how a large bank treats agent coordination as shared infrastructure, a model that engineering leaders can compare against their own setups.

sources.title: Inside Capital One’s multi-agent system

stories.headline: Will Larson's team-scale push reaches 170 merged PRs in one seven-day window
stories.summary: Will Larson reports shipping over 100 pull requests to production in a week, with 115 in the week of November 9 and a peak of 170 merged PRs over a seven-day period.
stories.why: A concrete throughput record gives leaders a real-world data point for judging delivery pace, though it is a single person's account.

sources.title: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week

stories.headline: Non-surgical brain scans and AI can reconstruct typed sentences
stories.summary: A Nature Neuroscience study reports that magnetic brain scans combined with AI can reconstruct typed sentences from outside the skull. Current brain implants that do this require risky neurosurgery.
stories.why: Non-invasive brain-to-text decoding could widen the range of interfaces and accessibility tools that engineers can build.

sources.title: Scientists at Meta decode typed sentences from brain activity without surgically implanted chips

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis about 2.5 years earlier, with the gap widening
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users develop psychosis an average of 2.5 years earlier than non-users. The gap grows to more than six years among adults aged 30 and older, and researchers warn the risks may build up over time.
stories.why: It adds evidence on long-term psychiatric risk, relevant to teams that handle wellbeing, health or safety features.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: Heavy smartphone use predicts a rebound in attention problems in late teens
stories.summary: A study tracking thousands of teenagers found attention symptoms tend to fall in early adolescence and then rise again as adulthood nears. Struggling to control smartphone use reliably predicted worse behavioural problems later.
stories.why: It gives product teams evidence on how self-control issues with phones relate to attention in young users.

sources.title: Problematic smartphone use predicts a rebound in attention issues during late adolescence

stories.headline: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental illness more than physical abuse
stories.summary: A Psychological Bulletin analysis of 104 studies found childhood emotional abuse is more strongly tied to adult mental illness than physical or sexual abuse. The authors argue it is often wrongly dismissed as less harmful because it leaves no visible marks.
stories.why: It is a reminder that harm without visible signs still has lasting effects, which matters when designing support and moderation systems.

sources.title: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental health struggles more strongly than physical or sexual abuse

stories.headline: Dell beats earnings on AI server demand and authorizes a $25 billion buyback
stories.summary: Dell reported third-quarter sales that more than doubled year on year, driven by AI server demand. The company also approved a $25 billion share buyback, and its shares rose.
stories.why: Strong AI server demand at a major hardware vendor signals continued heavy infrastructure spending by the companies that build and run AI workloads.

sources.title: Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback
Dell’s stock rises as the AI boom helps sales more than double

stories.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed in pharma's biggest deal in three years
stories.summary: Sanofi has agreed to acquire drugmaker Insmed, a deal described as the largest pharma acquisition in three years. Insmed shares rose about 14% on the news, while Sanofi faces falling revenue as key drugs lose exclusivity.
stories.why: Large pharma acquisitions drive demand for the data, regulatory and clinical software that companies in the sector rely on.

sources.title: Drugmaker Insmed shares rally 14% after Sanofi agrees to buy it in pharma’s biggest deal in three years

stories.headline: Xiamen Airlines to buy 50 Boeing 737-8 jets in deal worth about $7.4 billion
stories.summary: China's Xiamen Airlines has agreed to purchase 50 Boeing 737-8 aircraft. The order has a combined catalog price of around $7.4 billion.
stories.why: Large aircraft orders reflect airline capacity plans and the wider state of aerospace supply chains that depend on software and engineering services.

sources.title: China’s Xiamen Airlines to buy 50 Boeing jets in $7.4 billion deal

stories.headline: Budget carrier Norse Atlantic shares fall 77% after warning of critical finances
stories.summary: Norse Atlantic, a Norwegian low-cost airline, said its financial position is critical as fuel costs soar. Its survival depends on securing financing for short-term liquidity needs, and its shares dropped 77%.
stories.why: Rising fuel costs and funding strain at airlines can lead to cost cuts in travel and IT budgets, which affects vendors selling into the sector.

sources.title: Budget carrier Norse Atlantic falls 77% after warning its finances are ‘critical’ amid soaring fuel costs
